# sporewright

> Sporewright provides resilient pull-based work distribution over heterogeneous,
> transient, and non-deterministic actors. It ships a decision-equivalent Rust and
> TypeScript core under LGPL-3.0-only WITH LGPL-3.0-linking-exception,
> and is pre-1.0.

## Core model

A product declares an ordered address schema. Every exact prefix may contribute a
numeric residual for an option and dimension:

`Q(address, option, dimension) = sum(residual(prefix, option, dimension))`

Broader policy and belief therefore remain visible; deeper branches strengthen,
neutralize, or invert them rather than replacing them. Hard feasibility gates compose
by conjunction. Multi-objective scores use normalized lower-is-better dimensions and
additive path-composed weights.

The standard learned field is a hierarchical Gaussian model. Observations attach at
the realized address as natural sufficient statistics. Cached likelihood messages
update only the leaf-to-root path; a query sends cavity distributions only down its
requested path. Curiosity ranks by
`expected_score - temperature * sqrt(score_variance)` and a separate pure planner
enforces explicit execution-count and total-cost caps.

Routing receipts retain the field revision, exact address, alternatives, uncertainty,
contributing prefixes, and selected options. Retired subtrees can compact into exact
parent likelihood messages; explicit evidence discount lets product-owned clocks or
drift policy reopen uncertainty.

## Scale contract

- No address Cartesian product.
- No scan over unrelated workspaces, tasks, actors, or history.
- Resolve: `O(path declarations + depth * options * dimensions + options log options)`.
- Feedback: `O(address depth)`.
- Storage: explicitly declared/observed sparse parameter nodes; retired leaves can be
  compacted.

## Product boundary

Sporewright owns pure address traversal, residual composition, Gaussian messages,
curiosity math, receipts, compaction, serialization, work counters, writer authority,
and cross-core vectors. Products own vocabulary, normalization, variances, clocks,
deduplication, drift policy, hard budgets, candidate population, leases, execution,
persistence, authentication, and transport. A central orchestrator and a P2P product
use the same field algebra.

## Source map

- [README](https://github.com/corbet-foss/sporewright/blob/main/README.md)
- [Normative model](https://github.com/corbet-foss/sporewright/blob/main/docs/MODEL.md)
- [Routing guide](https://github.com/corbet-foss/sporewright/blob/main/docs/ROUTING-MODEL.md)
- [Scope](https://github.com/corbet-foss/sporewright/blob/main/SCOPE.md)
- Rust core: `crates/sporewright/src/field.rs`, `explore.rs`
- TypeScript core: `packages/sporewright/src/field.ts`, `explore.ts`
- Shared vectors: `tests/field-vectors/*.json`

The old `tensor` and `sync` modules remain temporarily for adopter migration. New
integrations use `field` and `explore`.

## Verification

- Rust: `cargo build --workspace && cargo test --workspace && cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- TypeScript core: in `packages/sporewright`, `bun test && bunx tsc --noEmit`
- LLM router: in `packages/router`, `bun test && bunx tsc --noEmit`
